'''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月夜見宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in Miyago, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">辰巳出版（2013）：16ページ</ref>. It is a [[:en:Betsugū|Betsugū]] of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Outer Shrine)<ref name="tm" /><ref name="ik">伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：39ページ</ref><ref name="mr">みらい出版（2013）：64ページ</ref><ref name="gk">学研パブリッシング（2013）：69ページ</ref><ref name="rg">JTBパブリッシング（2011）：42ページ</ref><ref name="rb">出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編（2014）：34ページ</ref><ref name="as">三橋（2013）：124ページ</ref>。 It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}.
== Overview ==
[[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]]
Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is an auxiliary shrine (betsugu) of the Outer Shrine (Geku), located about 300 meters north of Geku and approximately 500 meters west of {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise City Station}}. It enshrines two deities within the same shrine building: {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ツクヨミ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q595520}} (Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) and his fierce spirit, '''Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Aramitama''' (荒御魂 of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) <ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/>.
Unlike the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naikū)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naikū)|qq=}} auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naiku), where Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto and his Aramitama are enshrined separately, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya uniquely houses both deities within a single structure <ref name="rb"/>. The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaze-no-Miya|qq=}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-no-Miya|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命).
Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts <ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/><ref name="as"/>. Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere <ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/>. The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)}} <ref name="ik"/><ref name="gk"/>.
The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 37|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357923}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the '''Hatsuhobiki''' (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine.
Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社|comment=no clue what happened there|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takagawara Shrine|qq=}} <ref name="ik"/>. To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari Ōkami|ja|稲荷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q719665}} <ref name="tm"/>, and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers <ref name="rg"/>. Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a '''Shukueiya''' (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌).
== Worshipped Deities (Saijin) ==
{{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin|qq=}}}}
* {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|en|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}（つきよみのみこと）<ref name="tm"/><ref name="ik"/><ref name="mr"/><ref name="gk"/><ref name="rg"/><ref name="rb"/><ref name="as"/>
* {{nihongo|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Ara-Mitama|月夜見尊荒御魂}} <ref name="tm"/><ref name="ik"/><ref name="mr"/><ref name="gk"/><ref name="rg"/><ref name="rb"/><ref name="as"/>
: {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ツクヨミ}} is the same deity as {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月讀尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ツクヨミ}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naikū) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}.<ref name="mr"/><ref name="gk"/><ref name="rb"/><ref name="as"/> He is the brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}.<ref name="tm"/><ref name="gk"/><ref name="as"/> Since agricultural activities historically relied on the lunar calendar ({{ill|Lunar calendar|en|Lunar calendar|qid=Q185688|lt=Lunisolar calendar}}), he has been worshipped as a deity of agriculture.<ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/> Additionally, he is also considered a river deity of {{ill|Q23998361|ja|高河原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takagawara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q23998361}}<ref name="ik"/> and a deity associated with women.<ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/> According to the *{{ill|Jinmyō Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyō Hisho|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}*, his {{ill|Shintai|en|Shintai|qid=Q327532|lt=Shintai}} (sacred object) is a {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|qid=Q35197|lt=mirror}}.<ref name="as"/>
== Festivals ==
The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|qid=Q909452|lt=Imperial House of Japan}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinamisai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}* and *{{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}}*).
* '''January'''
**{{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}* (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|en|January 1|qid=Q2150|lt=January 1}}  
*** A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage.
**{{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai|qq=}}* (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|en|January 3|qid=Q2156|lt=January 3}}  
*** A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule.
* '''February'''
**{{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}* (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|en|February 11|qid=Q2335|lt=February 11}}  
*** Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}.
**{{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}}* (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|en|February 18|qid=Q2343|lt=February 18}}  
*** A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace.
**{{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}}* (Emperor’s Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|en|February 23|qid=Q2352|lt=February 23}}  
*** A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Naruhito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳仁|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q217096}}.
* '''May'''
**{{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|en|May 14|qid=Q2561|lt=May 14}}  
*** Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest.
* '''June'''
**{{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|en|June 18|qid=Q2670|lt=June 18}}–{{ill|June 19|en|June 19|qid=Q2669|lt=June 19}}  
*** A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭).
* '''August'''
**{{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|en|August 4|qid=Q2784|lt=August 4}}  
*** A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity.
* '''October'''
**{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}* (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|en|October 18|qid=Q2964|lt=October 18}}–{{ill|October 19|en|October 19|qid=Q2961|lt=October 19}}  
*** A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods.
* '''November'''
**{{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}}* (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|en|November 24|qid=Q3022|lt=November 24}}  
*** A festival in which the emperor offers the season’s first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude.
* '''December'''
**{{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|en|December 18|qid=Q2438|lt=December 18}}–{{ill|December 19|en|December 19|qid=Q2451|lt=December 19}}

* {{ill|March 1|en|March 1|qid=Q2393|lt=March 1}} - {{ill|Ōmike|ja|大御饌|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmike|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}（おおみけ）・{{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōhei|qq=}}
Above, the {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ritchūsai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|raising ceremony|ja|上棟祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōtōsai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上棟式|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q106351734}}, {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|杵築祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotsukisai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}}, {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|後鎮祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gochinsai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}}, {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengyo|qq=}}, and {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōhei|qq=}} were scheduled according to the divine decision (*{{ill|Gojijō|ja|御治定|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gojijō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}*) of the reigning emperor<ref name="sg"/>。 
Additionally, on {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|qid=Q2351|lt=February 22}}, the *{{ill|Oshiraishimochi|ja|お白石持|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshiraishi-mochi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17225061}}* ceremony took place, during which approximately 1,000 participants from the {{ill|Miyago Hōkendan|ja|宮後奉献団|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyago Hōkendan|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} carried sacred stones (*{{ill|Oshiraishi|ja|御白石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshiraishi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}*) in a cart from the {{ill|Urakuchi Intersection|ja|浦口交差点|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Urakuchi Intersection|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|2=ja|3=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=}}, covering a distance of 1.2 km<ref name="cn1502">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=次代につなぐ「エンヤ」 伊勢・月夜見宮でお白石持行事|author=中平雄大|publisher=[[中日新聞]]|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}</ref>。 This marked the Completion tier 5]]  
A '''narrow, 4-meter-wide straight path''' connects the '''North Gate (北御門, Kita-mikado) of the Outer Shrine''' to '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya'''. This road is known as '''"Kamiji Street" (神路通り, Kamiji-dōri), meaning "Path of the Gods,"''' as it is '''believed to be the route taken by deities.'''  
See {{ill|Kamiji Street|ja|神路通り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiji Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30114580}} for details.  
---
== Worshipers' Association (信者団体) ==
In '''1960 (Shōwa 35)''', a group of '''Ise City residents''' founded the '''Tsukiyomi-{{ill|Kō (lecture)|en|Kō (lecture)|qid=Q11632184|lt=kō}} (月夜見講)''', which was later renamed the '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya Hōsankai (月夜見宮奉賛会, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya Worshipers' Association).'''  
- This organization '''holds annual thanksgiving festivals''' on '''April 19 and September 19''', among other activities.  
---
== Access (交通) ==
* '''Train:'''
** '''10-minute walk''' from '''{{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise City Station}}''' (served by '''JR {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangu Line}}''' & '''Kintetsu {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Yamada Line}}''').  
** '''5-minute walk''' from the '''North Gate of the Outer Shrine''' via '''Kamiji Street'''.  
* '''Bus:'''
** '''3-minute walk''' from '''Shindō Bus Stop''' ('''{{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu}} Bus''').  
** '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop''' (served by the '''{{ill|Q11379021|ja|伊勢市コミュニティバス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Community Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379021}}''').  
** Note: From '''July 20, 2013''', the '''Sangu Bus''' operated by Mie Kotsu stopped at '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae''', but this service was '''discontinued on March 31, 2015'''.  
* '''Car:'''
** '''Approx. 3 km''' from '''{{ill|Ise interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884857}} (Ise Expressway).'''  
** '''Parking:''' There are '''only 2-4 parking spaces in front of the torii gate''', but '''metered parking''' is available on the south side of the street.

== Shrine Grounds (境内) ==
* '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (月夜見宮)''' - A '''Betsugū''' (auxiliary shrine) of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}). The shrine’s '''architecture follows Shinmei-zukuri''' and features '''chigi (forked finials) cut horizontally''' and '''five katsuogi (short decorative logs)''', '''a thatched roof''', and '''a south-facing orientation'''.  
** '''Shikinen Sengu (式年遷宮)''': The shrine is '''reconstructed every 20 years''' according to the ancient practice of '''Shikinen Sengu'''. The '''former shrine grounds''' (古殿地, kodenchi) are located directly to the east and west of the current shrine.  
** '''Traditional Legend''': It is said that in the past, when the people of '''Miyago Town''' were carrying '''sacred timber (役木, yakugi)''' for shrine reconstruction, they '''passed through Yokaichiba Town'''. At that moment, '''a fire broke out in Miyago Town''', and the timber carriers '''rushed back to extinguish it'''. As a result, the people of Yokaichiba took over the role of '''carrying the sacred timber'''. Since then, in the '''Okihikizome-shiki (御木曳初式, First Timber-Carrying Ceremony)''', '''the people of Yokaichiba''' have traditionally taken on the '''honor of bringing the sacred timber to Tsukiyomi-no-Miya'''.  
* '''{{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社|comment=no clue what happened there|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takagawara Shrine|qq=}}''' - Dedicated to '''Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama (月夜見尊御魂, Spirit of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto)'''. Though located within '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''', it is actually '''a Sessha (摂社, auxiliary shrine) of Toyōke Daijingū (Outer Shrine).'''  
* '''{{ill|Inari shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q514480}}''' – A shrine dedicated to '''Inari''', the deity of '''prosperity and agriculture'''.  
* '''Shukueya (宿衛屋)''' – A '''guardhouse''' for shrine officials.
